claims.statement: Deep Agents uses a trust-the-LLM model: an agent can do whatever its tools allow, so boundaries must be enforced at the tool or sandbox layer rather than by expecting the model to self-police.

FilesystemPermission applies ordered allow, deny, or interrupt rules to Deep Agents' built-in filesystem tools; unmatched calls are allowed, while direct backend usage is not covered by these permissions.

Filesystem permissions require absolute non-traversing patterns, remove denied paths from bulk read results, and use all-or-nothing overlap checks for recursive or potentially recursive deletion while retaining first-match behavior for a confirmed leaf.

Interrupt-mode filesystem rules are translated into human-in-the-loop predicates that distinguish exact and bulk tool scope, treat missing or current-directory bulk paths conservatively, check symlink targets when a backend is supplied, and prevent glob patterns from redirecting a search outside its path argument without review.

Deep Agents Code treats checked-out dotenv files as untrusted by blocking high-risk process-execution variables and project-level injection of MCP trust, Auto-review, subagent, and recursion controls; when the trusted global dotenv cannot be read, it skips project dotenv loading rather than assuming it is enabled.

Project MCP server trust is resolved only from managed or user-level configuration and selected process environment, not repository files; approvals bind a definition fingerprint to a repository or worktree as appropriate, while denies accumulate and malformed trust configuration is surfaced for fail-closed handling.

MCP OAuth storage uses safe server-derived token paths, in-process mutation locks, atomic replacement, and owner-only permission hardening where supported, but persists credential-bearing JSON that operators must treat as secret material.

Deep Agents Code binds a thread to a canonical server-resolved workspace and policy in SQLite; later runs reject unbound, substituted, fingerprint-mismatched, unsupported-schema, or identity-changed context, and bindings intentionally exclude secret model credentials and prompts from persisted workspace policy.

Thread-title generation treats conversation text as untrusted and limits the secondary model call to bounded visible human/AI content, excluding system, internal, control, and user-shell messages; it disables callbacks, uses a tool-free model, times out, and normalizes output.

For FilesystemBackend and routed FilesystemBackend paths, filesystem deny filtering checks both the requested path and its symlink-resolved target; resolution failures are denied or returned as errors, and bulk listings filter aliases resolving into denied trees.

FilesystemMiddleware rejects nonempty filesystem permissions on an execution-capable backend because execute has no permission enforcement, except when every rule is scoped to a CompositeBackend route prefix.

dcode's first Auto-mode enable displays a focused confirmation modal before activation, identifies the reviewing classifier—including when it differs from the coding model—and treats Enter as confirmation while Escape or programmatic dismissal cancels the switch; the notice is persisted only after confirmation and is versioned for once-per-install display.

Talon stores OAuth tokens, expiry, and client registration in a URL- and OAuth-configuration-derived credential file, serializes updates with a path lock, hardens its directory and temporary files, and atomically replaces the file; it preserves a refresh token omitted by a refresh response but not across a fresh grant, while warning that workspace placement and file permissions are not confidentiality boundaries against the default shell backend.

Talon validates OAuth discovery and provider metadata endpoints as safe public HTTPS URLs and sends them through an HTTPS-only, proxy-ignoring SSRF-safe transport with redirects disabled, bounded DNS and HTTP timeouts, and a 64 KiB JSON response limit; its transport maintains hostname-based Host and TLS validation while rejecting mixed public/private DNS resolution.

dcode's terminal-UI guidance treats external text as data: Rich markup uses escaped Content substitution or plain composition, externally sourced Markdown is line-normalized and escaped, dynamic notifications disable markup, and Auto-mode Markdown links are opened only through the shared URL safety check.
